paragraphs: Children in care in Carmarthenshire are looked after by Foster Wales Carmarthenshire, the county council's fostering service based at Ty Elwyn in Llanelli, and by the agencies listed on this page. The service is one of the 22 council fostering services that make up Foster Wales.

Llanelli is where the need is greatest. The council says that in 2023-24, 76 per cent of the children in foster care in Carmarthenshire came from Llanelli, and that many have to live away from their home town because there are not enough local carers. In August 2025 it launched a Fostering in Llanelli campaign, built on the message of local carers for local children, so that children can stay near their schools, friends and families. It says the need for carers continues across the whole county.

The council says the only firm requirement is a spare bedroom, and it welcomes people from every background, with or without experience. Training starts before approval with the Skills to Foster course and continues afterwards, and qualified social workers offer support 24 hours a day. Under its fostering payments framework, the council said in October 2025 that its carers receive between £351 and £942 a week, combining an allowance for the child's needs with a payment recognising the carer's skills and time. Carers also get free membership of The Fostering Network.
From 1 April 2026, the Welsh Government says new fostering providers in Wales must be not-for-profit. Speak to the council and the other services below, and compare their support and pay.
